calls.body: At home, the Blues keep sending Walker’s line (Toropchenko, Walker and Johnston) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Montgomery keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Stars’ fourth line is Kiviranta, Faksa and Perron.

calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is the league’s best, but St. Louis is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blues take could cost them.

surprises.head: Dallas brought the hits
surprises.body: Dallas usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 203 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 95 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 225 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Holloway has two goals and an assist as the Blues hold off the Stars
paras: Philip Broberg opened the scoring for the Blues just 26 seconds into the game, and Robert Thomas stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the first. Roope Hintz and Jason Robertson scored power-play goals just over a minute apart midway through the second to tie it 2-2. It was a busy third period. Robertson scored his second of the night early in the period to put the Stars ahead 3-2, but they didn’t score again. Dylan Holloway made it 3-3 for St. Louis on the power play later in the period, and Aleksanteri Kaskimäki put the Blues ahead for good three and a half minutes later. Holloway scored again into the empty net with just under a minute left. Four players had three-point nights: Thomas with a goal and two assists, Jake Neighbours with three assists, Holloway with two goals and an assist, and Robertson with two goals and an assist.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Joel Hofer made 25 saves for the Blues, and Casey DeSmith stopped 15 of 19 at the other end. The Blues moved to 14-9-3, sixth in the Central, while the Stars fell to 15-8-2, slipping to fourth in the Central.

items.text: The Blues have points in six straight games (5-0-1).
The Stars scored on the power play for the first time since Nov 14, after going 0-for-10 over five games.
Wyatt Johnston has a point in seven straight games.
With Jimmy Snuggerud out, Neighbours took his spot and had three assists.
